Pattern Matching

This page collects all of SLA's "take a value by shape" spellings: match/switch, if let chains, let else, while let, and the recently added struct update Struct { ..base } and slice rest pattern [a, b, ..rest]. All examples are from real demos.

The match expression

match branches on an enum value by variant, and payloads can be destructured and bound directly (demos/rosetta/06_enum_and_match/main.sla):

enum Message {
    Quit,
    Move { x: i32, y: i32 },
}

fn process_msg(msg: Message) -> i32 {
    match msg {
        Message::Quit => {
            return 0;
        },
        Message::Move { x, y } => {
            return x + y;
        },
    };
}

Tuple-like (tuple variants) are destructured by position (demos/rosetta/43_tagged_union/main.sla):

enum Shape {
    Circle(i32),
    Square(i32),
}

fn area(shape: Shape) -> i32 {
    match shape {
        Shape::Circle(r) => { r * r * 3 },
        Shape::Square(s) => { s * s },
    }
}
NoteMatch extraction of enum payloads is not yet fully covered on the direct SAB fast path; when hit, the SAB path errors loudly (with no silent fallback); see the Feature Maturity Matrix page for details.

The switch statement

switch does flat branching on integer values (compiled to an eq + br branch ladder):

switch status {
    200 => { return current_config + sum; },
    500 => { return -1; },
    default => { return 0; }
}

if let chains, let else, and while let

All three are built on the same pattern classification (Option/Result/user enum tags). The following are from demos 104, 105, and 136 respectively:

// if let 链
let result = if let Some(x) = left && let Some(y) = middle && let Some(z) = right {
    x + y + z
} else {
    0
};

// let else：模式不匹配时进入 else 块并必须发散
let Some(x) = value else {
    println("{}", 0);
    return 0;
};

// while let
while let Some(task) = queue.pop() {
    let resolved = task.await;
    total = total + resolved;
}

Tuple and array destructuring

// 元组解构（demos/rosetta/12_destructuring）
let (x, y) = (2, 5);

// 数组 rest 解构 + 丢弃绑定（demos/rosetta/310_blank_identifier_discard）
let [_, second, ..rest] = [10, 20, 30, 40];
let (w2, _) = (7, 8);
return second + rest[0] + w2;

_ is a discard binding: the right-hand value is constructed and then immediately cleaned up by compiler-managed lifetime handling, producing no unused warning.

Struct update: Struct { ..base }

A struct literal may end with ..base to inherit the fields not explicitly listed from an existing value; this is a pure frontend rewrite and introduces no runtime dispatch (demos/syntax_sugar/struct_update/main.sla):

struct SpawnConfig {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    layer: i32,
    visible: bool,
}

fn move_to_next_layer(config: SpawnConfig) -> SpawnConfig {
    return SpawnConfig {
        layer: config.layer + 1,
        ..config
    };
}
WarningStruct update copies the fields of base that are not replaced into the new value. The updated original value is afterwards handled by the compiler's managed lifetime cleanup; do not assume the fields were moved out.

Related pages: Structs and Enums, Feature Maturity Matrix.
